RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.label: lab notes
RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.description: What was done at the gate, in order, with the numbers. The company reads these to decide whether a branch is following procedure or improvising, so they are wanted for every recorded step rather than only the ones that went wrong.\n\nWritten at a records desk from the step's own record. Nothing is invented at the desk; if the step was not recorded, there is nothing to write up.

RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.label: investigation
RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.description: An account of what the crew found and where, filed once the record book is in the branch's custody on an archive shelf. The company will not accept an investigation written from memory while the book is still in somebody's pack.\n\nThis is the paperwork that turns a recovered book into a case the company recognises.

RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.label: analysis
RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.description: The findings, written up after a researcher has actually analysed the record. The analysis is the work; this is the report the company is paying to read.\n\nIt cannot be written before the analysis finishes, which is the whole reason it is a separate piece of paperwork rather than part of the bench job.

RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.label: research write-up
RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.description: What a finished company project actually established, in language the corporation's own people can act on. A branch that learns something and files nothing has spent its insight privately.\n\nWanted once the project is complete, and only then.

RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.label: survey report
RimroomsAsyncIndustries.Company.Rimrooms.description: The finished map of a coordinate: every room the crew entered, how they connect, and what was in them. Filed once a space has been explored end to end, not room by room.\n\nThis is the deliverable a completed survey produces, and it is what the company pays for when it buys a map it did not have.
